item.title: 3 dead after NBC Los Angeles news helicopter crashes in Chatsworth
item.description: The crash happened near the spot of a deadly Metro bus crash in Chatsworth.

item.title: House votes to limit Trump's Iran war powers for a third time
item.description: The House voted for a third time to restrict President Trump's power to strike Iran. Meanwhile, GOP Rep. Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. CBS News' Eleanor Watson reports.

item.title: Kennedy Center Board votes to close for renovations amid legal fight over Trump name
item.description: A judge blocked President Trump's name from being added to the Kennedy Center facade again on Tuesday. Later in the day, the institution's board voted to close the venue for renovations. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi explains.

item.title: Maye Musk talks modeling career, escaping an abusive relationship and being Elon's mom
item.description: Maye Musk, supermodel and mother to Elon Musk, joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss her new memoir, "Timeless: The Art of Reinvention and Resilience at Any Age."

item.title: How the FBI's counterterrorism mission has evolved since 9/11
item.description: FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia discusses how the bureau has expanded its counterterrorism resources since the 9/11 attacks, the evolving nature of threats, and Iran's use of asymmetric warfare tactics.

item.title: Fed rate hike expected on Wednesday. See what it means for your money.
item.description: The Federal Reserve is likely to raise borrowing costs on Wednesday, and more hikes could be in store, according to economists.

item.title: Why the Fed might raise interest rates for first time since 2023
item.description: The Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in three years on Wednesday. CBS News business contributor Javier David explains more.

item.title: An exclusive look inside Zelenskyy's wartime office
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke to CBS News' Aidan Stretch in an exclusive interview at his wartime office. Zelenskyy said he believes Russian President Vladimir Putin is lying about wanting peace and an end to the Russia-Ukraine war.

item.title: Andrew Huberman on small changes that can make a big difference
item.description: Andrew Huberman, a neuroscientist at Stanford University School of Medicine and host of "The Huberman Lab" podcast, joins "CBS Mornings" to talk about his new book, "Protocols: An Operating Manual for the Human Body."

item.title: OpenAI chief says "we've entered a new phase" of AI capabilities
item.description: Chris Lehane, the chief global affairs officer for OpenAI, joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss recent tech leaders' efforts to address AI safety and regulations.

item.title: AI "self-regulation is a joke," Pro-Human Assembly organizer says
item.description: Artificial intelligence regulation has become a political flashpoint, with expert whistleblowers, frontier tech CEOs and some bipartisan politicians calling for government oversight. Meanwhile, President Trump has dismissed concerns that AI could threaten humanity. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns reports, and MIT professor and AI activist Max Tegmark shares his thoughts.

item.title: Kendra Scott says joining "Shark Tank" is "a natural fit"
item.description: Designer Kendra Scott, who started her billion-dollar jewelry empire with $500, sits down with "CBS Mornings" to talk about joining "Shark Tank" full time.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed blasts GOP opponent Mike Rogers for skipping Michigan Senate debate
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed blasted his Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, for skipping their debate Tuesday night. CBS News' political director Fin Gómez has more on this and other races.

item.title: Mike Rogers speaks out after skipping Michigan Senate debate
item.description: The Republican says the event was a town hall he never committed to and was never on his schedule. He also faulted the moderator, saying you can't hold a "two-on-one event in a TV studio."

item.title: House votes to limit Trump's power to strike Iran for 3rd time
item.description: The previous votes have failed to stop President Trump from waging war with Iran.

item.title: White House backs Hegseth as new details come out about Iran war's cost
item.description: The Iran war has cost the U.S. military at least $33.4 billion — most of it on munitions — and not including hundreds of millions more spent by other agencies, the Pentagon says.

item.title: U.S. soldier says we're "getting punched in the face" after photos of damage caused by Iran emerge
item.description: CBS News obtained new images of damaged buildings and equipment at U.S. positions in the Middle East. This comes amid renewed scrutiny surrounding military resource management and Iran war spending. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan has more.

item.title: Can a debt relief company help after you've been sued for unpaid debt?
item.description: A debt lawsuit can raise the stakes quickly, but you may still have a few options for dealing with what you owe.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Board votes to close Kennedy Center immediately for renovations, source says
item.description: Earlier Tuesday, a federal judge again blocked the board from adding President Trump's name to the facade of the building.

item.title: Ed Sheeran speaks out on dropping Macklemore from tour, says it was promoters' decision
item.description: Ed Sheeran spoke out Tuesday after facing backlash for dropping Macklemore from his tour following the rapper's pro-Palestinian statements onstage. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is "ready for energy ceasefire" with Russia
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke exclusively with CBS News' Aidan Stretch, where he discussed his country's ongoing war with Russia.

item.title: Family blames Texas' "merciless" abortion ban for woman's death, sues Paxton, others
item.description: The family of 37-year-old Tierra Walker filed a lawsuit against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and others, saying she was denied an abortion that could have saved her life.

item.title: U.S. adds sanctions on South Africa, alleging discrimination against White people
item.description: The Trump administration has announced that it will impose travel bans on officials it claims are responsible for discrimination against White people and other minority groups in South Africa.

item.title: How Olympian Aly Raisman learned to advocate for her own health
item.description: In the latest episode of "Healthful," Olympic gold medalist Aly Raisman discusses what she's learned about speaking up for herself and taking care of her body.

item.title: In Washington, unlikely bedfellows like Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon talk about making AI "humans first"
item.description: As AI CEOs call for a slowdown, President Trump wants acceleration. But the issue is gaining bipartisan momentum.

item.title: Ed Sheeran's supporting acts pull out of tour after Macklemore was dropped
item.description: Aaron Rowe, Beoga, Lukas Graham and Finneas all released statements Tuesday on Instagram saying they were withdrawing from Ed Sheeran's tour.

item.title: Own a car? You're getting socked by higher prices, and not only for gas
item.description: Car ownership costs have soared 50% since 2020, according to new economic data. Here's where motorists are getting dinged.

item.title: OpenAI backs measure that would require independent audits of AI models
item.description: Top OpenAI executive endorses plan that would require AI companies to submit their technology to third-party reviews to assess their safety.

item.title: Americans' incomes hit a record high in 2025. Now for the bad news.
item.description: The typical U.S. household's annual earnings have risen only 2.5% since 2019, new data from the Census Bureau shows.
